correctness.rationale: For each fixed labeled degree tuple, every input homogeneous component is zero- or one-dimensional and every output lies in a zero- or one-dimensional homogeneous component. If two or more nonzero degree counts are odd, the total degree is outside the support, forcing zero. If at most one is odd, an explicit bracketing pairs equal basis vectors, using \(v_i^2=\beta(v_i,v_i)1\ne0\), and gives a nonzero evaluation, so the quotient dimension is exactly one. Character orthogonality on \((\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)^n\) then gives the closed formula. The checker independently confirms the combinatorial count for \(1\le n\le6\), \(1\le m\le8\). Risk: the statement depends on the standard definition of total multilinear graded codimension as the direct sum over labeled degree assignments; this definition is made explicit in RESULT.md.

value.rationale: The result converts a recent structural description of fine-graded identities into a complete, closed, field-independent multilinear growth law. It gives every finite-rank codimension, an immediate exact Klein-grading sequence for symmetric 2x2 matrices, and the graded growth exponent equal to the algebra dimension. This is a natural invariant in PI theory rather than an arbitrary finite slice; the formula is usable for asymptotics and comparison across fields.
